newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia-IMF talks seen difficult, statement soon.
newsitem.headline: Russia-IMF talks seen difficult, statement soon.

text.p: Discussions between Russia and the International Monetary Fund are difficult and the two sides plan to issue a statement on Thursday or Friday, sources close to the talks said.

One Russian official said tax collection was the key issue dividing the two sides as the IMF assesses whether to release the latest tranche of a $10 billion three-year loan. The IMF, whose delegation is expected to leave Moscow at the end of this week, declined to comment.
The IMF postponed paying one tranche of the loan during the summer because it was not satisfied at Russia's ability to meet its 1996 budget plans.
Russian officials have said the federal budget deficit is now within the forecast range, but economists say this is because the government has virtually stopped spending money.
Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin said on Tuesday he hoped the IMF would not delay payment of the next tranche the loan, saying to do so would be "very unjust."

"If we take as a base the formal requirements it is clear that this is possible, but in the situation which Russia is in I think it would be a very unjust thing," Yasin told Reuters during a visit to Milan.
